---
title: "EXP-0001 — SiRA simulative versus reactive protocol"
---

## Current state

`EXP-0001` is **planned**, its evidence is **not evaluated**, and its outcome is
**pending**. No smoke, pilot, model, API, browser, evaluator, or benchmark run has
occurred. Execution authorization is false.

## Locked exploratory comparison

The treatment is exactly `SIRA-SIMULATIVE`; the control is exactly `SIRA-REACTIVE`.
Both are assigned externally by the experiment. The assignment is not evidence of a
learned internal regulation mechanism.

The smoke is one minimal matched pair on the pinned README query and prohibits
interpretation. The pilot is two counterbalanced FanOutQA task pairs selected only to
exercise paired execution, deterministic scoring, and variance plumbing. It is not an
effect-size-based sample and cannot support a confirmatory or adequately powered
claim.

The historical upstream run used the mutable `gpt-4o` alias without an immutable
serving revision. The proposed protocol substitutes a dated GPT-4o snapshot. Any later
evidence must therefore be called a **directional reproduction under a declared model
substitution**, never an unqualified reproduction.

## Evidence and future-track boundary

Raw traces, commands, configuration, environment identity, timestamps, hashes, costs,
and cleanup evidence are retained before normalization. Public raw release remains
blocked pending licensing, privacy, and redaction review.

The protocol also retains source-grounded regulation-decision provenance for the
planned/deferred `RQ-H2K` track. This is an additive evidence-preservation appendix,
not an EXP-0001 hypothesis, metric, outcome, treatment, control, ablation, training
condition, or interpretation. Trace sufficiency supports only source classification
and lineage; it does not support internalization.

See the generated [experiment registry](../generated/experiments.qmd) for canonical
lifecycle, evidence, and outcome state.
